definition: A solid in which atoms are joined by covalent bonds in a continuous network through the whole structure, with no separate molecules, so melting it means breaking strong covalent bonds.
One of two or more structural forms of the same element in the same physical state, such as diamond and graphite, or $\ce{O2}$ and $\ce{O3}$.
Electrons that are not confined to one atom or one bond, but are shared over several or many atoms and can move among them.
